bot_doi.mo_ta: The long distant wooded landmass across the upper-right horizon has been removed and replaced by open sea.
The original broad grassy coastal plain has been cut away across the centre and right, moving the shore dramatically inland.
The Rock's lower silhouette and terrain geometry have been reshaped into a much more extensive cliff-fronted headland; this exceeds a texture change.

The long original defensive wall remains near its original screen position, but the land supporting it has become a cliff or water-facing edge, leaving parts apparently suspended over the rebuilt terrain.
Original tree and scrub groups along the former middle-distance shoreline have disappeared beneath the expanded sea.
Original isolated trees and vegetation patches in the upper-right inland plain have been removed by the coastline replacement.
The original left foreground trees have been removed or replaced by pasture, animals, paths and different vegetation.
The original dense right-hand grove has been substantially rearranged, with individual tree positions, shapes and count changed.
Small rectangular bare or cultivated plots in the middle-left plain have been erased or replaced by paths and vegetation.
The original faint curved track on the lower-right has been replaced by a broader, differently routed winding dirt path.

doi_loai_vung.mo_ta: LAND TO WATER: the distant landmass along the upper-right horizon is completely replaced by sea.
LAND TO WATER: the former flat coastal plain between the original shoreline and the new left-central beach becomes part of the bay.
LAND TO WATER: a very large portion of the middle-right plain becomes sea, from the former shoreline down to the new diagonal coast.
LAND TO WATER: the ground surrounding the distant right-hand camp strip is removed, making the retained rectangular camp appear to project into or float over the sea.
WATER TO LAND: parts of the original small inlet below the Rock are filled by the new settlement, rocky headland and beach.
